title: .gitignore
summary: A .gitignore file lists files git should leave alone, like logs, build output and secrets.

levels.title: Ignore a file
levels.briefing: Some files should never be committed. Each line of a .gitignore file is a name or pattern; matching files stop showing up as untracked, and git add skips them. The .gitignore itself is committed so everyone shares the same rules.
levels.objective: Make git ignore debug.log, then commit your .gitignore.

cheatsheet.description: Pattern: an exception to an earlier rule

hints: Create a file called .gitignore containing the name to ignore.
After that, debug.log disappears from git status. Commit .gitignore.
Run: echo debug.log > .gitignore, git add .gitignore, git commit -m "Ignore log"
levels.successMessage: debug.log stays in your folder, but git no longer offers to track it.

levels.title: Every log file
levels.objective: Ignore every file ending in .log (but not app.js), then commit your .gitignore.
hints: Run: echo "*.log" > .gitignore, git add .gitignore, git commit -m "Ignore logs"
levels.successMessage: Patterns let one line ignore any number of matching files.

levels.title: A whole folder
levels.objective: Ignore everything in the build folder, then commit your .gitignore.
hints: A pattern ending in / matches a folder.
Ignoring the folder ignores everything inside it.
Run: echo "build/" > .gitignore, git add .gitignore, git commit -m "Ignore build"
levels.successMessage: Build output can always be recreated, so it is normally ignored.

levels.title: An exception
levels.objective: Ignore every .tmp file except keep.tmp, then commit your .gitignore.
hints: Ignore *.tmp first, then add an exception on the next line.
A line starting with ! un-ignores a file.
Run: echo "*.tmp" > .gitignore, echo "!keep.tmp" >> .gitignore, git add .gitignore, git commit -m "Ignore tmp"
levels.successMessage: Later lines win, so the ! rule makes an exception to the *.tmp rule above it.
